title: winddown
subtitle: One command to end the developer day.
body:
For developers running several Claude Code sessions who find it hard to stop.
AI makes each task faster, so we take on more, and the evenings go.

caption: 19:45. Two repos, both with unfinished work.

steps.out:
e85414f add streaming parser
ee507e5 add CSV parser

caption:
One command closes the day.
(--no-kill only so this recording does not stop the agent filming it.)

steps.out: Closed 2 repos, stashed 2, tomorrow's list is in TOMORROW.md. You're done until 08:30.

caption: Your work is stashed safely. Commits are untouched.

steps.out:
On branch main
nothing to commit, working tree clean

caption: Tomorrow's list: at most 3 items, built from your real diff and commits.

steps.out:
# Tomorrow

**Where you stopped:** editing src/parser.py, tests/test_parser.py, stashed as "winddown 2026-10-29 20:28".

1. Restore your work: `git stash pop --index stash@{0}` (src/parser.py, tests/test_parser.py)
2. FIXME: skips the last line in src/parser.py:6
3. Continue from today's last commit: "add streaming parser"

caption:
22:10. You open Claude Code for "just one more thing".
Its UserPromptSubmit hook runs winddown check:

steps.cmd: echo '{"prompt":"one more fix"}' | winddown check; echo "exit code: $?"
steps.out:
Winddown active until 08:30. Rest. Run `winddown resume` to override.
exit code: 2

caption:
Exit code 2 means Claude Code blocks the prompt. The evening stays yours.
Next morning the pause lifts at 08:30 by itself. Or, any time:

title: No alerts. No dashboards. No prompts.
subtitle: It runs once, prints one line, and gives the evening back.
